rdl_0001.question: What is round as a dishpan, deep as a tub, and still the oceans couldn't fill it up?

rdl_0002.question: You are on a ship, over the side hangs a rope ladder with half meter rungs. The tide rises a half meter per hour. At the end of five hours, how much of the ladder will remain above the water assuming that nine rungs were above the water when the tide began to rise?
rdl_0002.answer: Remember the tde Nine rungs will be above the water. As the tide rises, so will the ship and the ladder

rdl_0003.question: I have many feathers to help me fly. I have a body and head, but I'm not alive. It is your strength which determines how far I go. You can hold me in your hand, but I'm never thrown. What am I?

rdl_0004.question: I'm in the book, but not on any leaf; I'm in the mouth, but not in lip or teeth; I'm in the atmosphere, but never in the air; I wait on every one, but never on a pair; I am with you wherever you may go; And every thing you do I'm sure to know; Though when you did it I should not be there, Yet when 'twas done, you'd find me in the chair. What am I ?

rdl_0005.question: I'm as small as an ant, as big as a whale. I'll approach like a breeze but can come like a gale. By some, I get hit, but all have shown fear. I'll dance to the music, though I can't hear. Of names, I have many, of names I have one. I'm as slow as a snail, but from me, you can't run. What am I ?

rdl_0006.question: What God never sees, what the king seldom sees, and what we see every day. What is it? Read my riddle .

rdl_0007.question: What can be heard and caught but never seen?

rdl_0008.question: Not born, but from a Mother's body drawn, I hang until half of me is gone. I sleep in a cave until I grow old, then valued for my hardened gold. What am I?

rdl_0009.question: Black I am and much admired, men seek me until they're tired. When they find me, they break my head, and take from me my resting bed. What am I?

rdl_0010.question: I am as light as a feather, yet no man can hold me for long. What am I ?

rdl_0011.question: I am not alive, but I grow; I don't have lungs, but I need air; I don't have a mouth, but water kills me. What am I ?

rdl_0012.question: I was carried into a dark room and set on fire. I wept, and then my head was cut off. What am I?

rdl_0013.question: This old one runs forever but never moves at all. It has not lungs nor throat, but still a mighty roaring call. What is it?

rdl_0014.question: I pass before the sun, yet make no shadow. What am I ?

rdl_0015.question: I killed one fourth of all mankind. Who am I?

rdl_0016.question: Why are your nose and chin always at variance?
rdl_0016.answer: Because words are passing between them.

rdl_0017.question: It speaks with a hard tongue, it cannot breathe, for it has no lungs. What is it?

rdl_0018.question: Why ought a fisherman to be very wealthy?
rdl_0018.answer: Because his is all net profit.

rdl_0019.question: How high would you have to count before you would use the letter A in the English language spelling of a whole number?

rdl_0020.question: We are little creatures; all of us have different features. One of us in glass is set; one of us you'll find in jet. Another you may see in tin, and the fourth is boxed within. If the fifth you should pursue, it can never fly from you. What are we?

rdl_0021.question: If you're 8 feet away from a door and with each move you advance half the distance to the door. How many moves will it take to reach the door?
rdl_0021.answer: Infinity! Technically you will never reach the door, as you can only move half the distance, no matter how small.

rdl_0022.question: There is an ancient invention, still used in some parts of the world today, that allows people to see through walls. What is it?

rdl_0023.question: Tom and his younger sister were fighting. Their mother was tired of the fighting and decided to punish them by making them stand on the same piece of newspaper in such a way that they couldn't touch each other. How did she accomplish this?
rdl_0023.answer: Tom's mother slid a newspaper under a door, each sibling standing on each side.

rdl_0024.question: I am a rock group that has 4 members, all of whom are dead, one of which was assasinated. What am I?
rdl_0024.answer: Mount Rushmore. Get it, rock group?

rdl_0025.question: The answer I give is yes, but what I mean is no. What was the question?

rdl_0026.question: I have a heart that never beats, I have a home but I never sleep. I can take a man's house and build another, And I love to play games with my many brothers. I am a king among fools. Who am I ?
rdl_0026.answer: The King of Hearts in a deck of cards.

rdl_0027.question: With pointed fangs it sits in wait, With piercing force it doles out fate, Over bloodless victims proclaiming its might, Eternally joining in a single bite. What is it?

rdl_0028.question: What is red and blue, and purple and green, No one can reach it, not even a Queen?

rdl_0029.question: Four cars come to a four-way stop, all coming from a different direction. They can't decide who got there first, so they all go forward at the same time. They do not crash into each other, but all four cars go. How is this possible?

rdl_0030.question: Where do Turkeys go to dance?

rdl_0031.question: I cover what's real, hide what is true, but sometimes bring out the courage in you. What am I?

rdl_0032.question: Why is a man in debt like a misty morning?
rdl_0032.answer: Because he is surrounded with dues (dews).

rdl_0033.question: I have a big mouth and I am also quite loud! I am NOT a gossip but I do get involved with everyone's dirty business. What am I?

rdl_0034.question: Who makes it, has no need of it. Who buys it, has no use for it. Those who use it can neither see nor feel it. What is it?

rdl_0035.question: What goes through the door without pinching itself, sits on the stove without burning itself, sits on the table, and is not ashamed?

rdl_0036.question: What work is it that the faster you work, the longer it is before you're done, and the slower you work, the sooner you're finished?

rdl_0037.question: I give you a group of three. One is sitting down, and will never get up. The second eats as much as is given to him, yet is always hungry. The third goes away and never returns. What are the three things?

rdl_0038.question: I know a word of letters three. Add two, and fewer there will be. What is it?

rdl_0039.question: Five hundred begins it, five hundred ends it, five in the middle is seen; first of all figures, the first of all letters, take up their stations between. Join all together, and then you will bring before you the name of an eminent king. Who is it?

rdl_0040.question: I build up castles. I tear down mountains. I make some men blind, I help others to see. What am I?

rdl_0041.question: Lovely and round, I shine with pale light, grown in the darkness, A lady's delight. What am I?

rdl_0042.question: At the sound of me, men may dream, Or stamp their feet. At the sound of me, women may laugh , Or sometimes weep. What am I?

rdl_0043.question: You can see nothing else When you look in my face, I will look you in the eye and I will never lie. What am I?

rdl_0044.question: You heard me before, Yet you hear me again, Then I die, 'Till you call me again. What am I?

rdl_0045.question: My life can be measured in hours, I serve by being devoured. Thin, I am quick. Fat, I am slow. Wind is my foe. What am I ?

rdl_0046.question: Weight in my belly, Trees on my back. Nails in my ribs, Feet I do lack. What am I?

rdl_0047.question: Three lives have I. Gentle enough to soothe the skin, Light enough to caress the sky, Hard enough to crack rocks. What am I?

rdl_0048.question: Lighter than what I am made of, more of me is hidden than is seen. What am I?

rdl_0049.question: If a man carried my burden he would break his back. I am not rich, but leave silver in my track. What am I?

rdl_0050.question: I am only useful when I am full, yet I am always full of holes. What am I?

rdl_0051.question: I am always hungry, I must always be fed, The finger I touch will soon turn red. What am I?

rdl_0052.question: I'm not really more than holes tied to more holes; I'm strong as good steel, though not as stiff as a pole. What am I?

rdl_0053.question: Whoever makes it, tells it not. Whoever takes it, knows it not. And whoever knows it wants it not. What is it?

rdl_0054.question: What gets wetter the more it dries?

rdl_0055.question: What kind of running means walking?

rdl_0056.question: Two words, my answer is only two words . To keep me, you must give me. What am I?

rdl_0057.question: What goes up when the rain comes down?

rdl_0058.question: Walk on the living, they don't even mumble. Walk on the dead, they mutter and grumble. What are they?

rdl_0060.question: What word contains all of the twenty six letters?

rdl_0061.question: There was a man who was born before his father, killed his mother , and married his sister. Yet, there was nothing wrong with what he had done. Why?
rdl_0061.answer: His father was in front of him when he was born, therefore he was born before him. His mother died while giving birth to him. Finally, he grew up to be a minister and married his sister at her ceremony.

rdl_0062.question: What 4-letter word can be written forward, backward or upside down, and can still be read from left to right?

rdl_0063.question: A large truck is crossing a bridge 1 mile long. The bridge can only hold 14000 lbs, which is the exact weight of the truck. The truck makes it half way across the bridge and stops. A bird lands on the truck. Does the bridge collapse?
rdl_0063.answer: No, it does not collapse. Because it has driven a half mile - you would subtract the gas used from the total weight of the truck.

rdl_0064.question: I'm sometimes white, Although sometimes I'm black. I take you there, But never bring you back. What am I?

rdl_0065.question: You are in a room that is completely bricked in on all four sides, including the ceiling and floor. You have nothing but a mirror and a wooden table in the room with you. How do you get out?
rdl_0065.answer: You look in the mirror you see what you saw, you take the saw and you cut the table in half, two halves make a whole, and you climb out the hole.

rdl_0066.question: The rungs of a 10-foot ladder attached to a ship are 1 foot apart. If the water is rising at the rate of one foot an hour, how long will it take until the water covers the ladder?
rdl_0066.answer: It will never cover the ladder because as the water rises, so will the floating ship.

rdl_0067.question: A sign on the barber's door says "I shave only those who do not shave themselves". Does the barber shave himself?
rdl_0067.answer: There is no answer; it's a paradox. It cannot be made to work.

rdl_0068.question: Two girls have the same parents and were born at the same hour on the same day of the same month, but they are not twins. How can this be possible?
rdl_0068.answer: They were not born in the same year.

rdl_0069.question: A pregnant lady named her children : Dominique, Regis, Michelle, Fawn, Sophie, and Lara. What will she name her next child? Jessica, Katie, Abby, or Tilly?
rdl_0069.answer: Tilly. She seems to follow the scale Do, Re, Me, Fa, So, La, and then Ti.

rdl_0070.question: A pet shop owner had a parrot with a sign on its cage that said "Parrot repeats everything it hears." A young man bought the parrot and for two weeks he spoke to it and it didn't say a word. He returned the parrot but the shopkeeper said he never lied about the parrot. How can this be?

rdl_0071.question: A woman was horrified to find a fly in her tea. The waiter took her cup and went into the kitchen and returned with a fresh cup of tea. She shouted, "You brought me the same tea!" How did she know?
rdl_0071.answer: She had already put sugar in it and when she tasted the new tea it was already sweet.

rdl_0072.question: Which word in the English language becomes shorter when it is lengthened?

rdl_0073.question: If you have three oranges and you take away two, how many will you have?

rdl_0074.question: What's the least number of chairs you would need around a table to sit four fathers, two grandfathers, and four sons?
rdl_0074.answer: Four. The trick is that the roles overlap. You only need four chairs because the same four people can simultaneously satisfy “four fathers,” “two grandfathers,” and “four sons.” A classic arrangement is: great‑grandfather, grandfather, father, and son. In this setup: The great‑grandfather and the grandfather are both grandfathers. All four can be fathers (the son can have a child not present). All four are also sons of someone. So the least number of chairs is four

rdl_0075.question: Look at me. I can bring a smile to your face, A tear to your eye, Or even a thought to your mind. But, I can't be seen. What am I?

rdl_0076.question: You do not want to have it, But when you do have it, You do not want to lose it. What is it?

rdl_0077.question: My first is often at the front door. My second is found in the cereal family. My third is what most people want. My whole is one of the United States. What am I?
rdl_0077.answer: MATRIMONY (mat rye money). Which is certainly a "united state"!

rdl_0078.question: What is more useful when it is broken?

rdl_0079.question: There is a frog, dead in the middle of an island. If he swims north, the distance to the mainland is 2 meters. If he swims south, the distance to the mainland is 3 meters. If he swims east or west, the distance is 4 meters. Which way does he swim?
rdl_0079.answer: He doesn't swim at all, he is dead.

rdl_0080.question: You live in a one story house made entirely of redwood. What color would the stairs be?
rdl_0080.answer: What stairs? You live in a one-story house.

rdl_0081.question: I can be created by humans, But they cannot control me. I suck on wood, paper and flesh alike. I can be more of a hindrance than help at times. To my creators, I seem to be everywhere at once. What am I?

rdl_0082.question: I am the fountain from which no one can drink. For many I am considered a necessary link. Like gold to all I am sought for, But my continued death brings wealth for all to want more. What am I?

rdl_0083.question: I fly in the air, But I am not always there. I cannot be touched, But I can be felt or held. Think very hard, But if you live near the equator, You may have a tough time seeing me. What am I?

rdl_0084.question: A man was shot to death while in his car. There were no powder marks on his clothing, which indicated that the gunman was outside the car. However, all the windows were up and the doors locked. After a close inspection was made, the only bullet holes discovered were on the man's body. How was he murdered?
rdl_0084.answer: The victim was in a convertible. He was shot when the top was down.

rdl_0085.question: I am one with eight to spare, lest I lose my one. I'm not a number. What am I?

rdl_0086.question: Which bird does not belong in this group? Finch, gull, eagle, ostrich, or sparrow?
rdl_0086.answer: The Ostrich. It's the only bird that doesn't fly.

rdl_0087.question: Where on Earth do the winds always blow from the South?

rdl_0088.question: What can you throw but not catch?

rdl_0089.question: Which word can be placed between the two following words to make two new ones: TABLE _ _ _ _ HOUSE?

rdl_0090.question: A certain crime is punishable if attempted but not punishable if committed. What is it?

rdl_0091.question: How many letters are in the alphabet ?
rdl_0091.answer: There are 11 letters in "THE ALPHABET." Did you say 26?

rdl_0092.question: You use a knife to slice my head and weep beside me when I am dead. What am I?

rdl_0093.question: I never was, am always to be, No one ever saw me, nor ever will, And yet I am the confidence of all to live and breathe on this terrestrial ball. What am I ?

rdl_0094.question: From the beginning of eternity To the end of time and space From the beginning of every end And the end of every place. What am I?

rdl_0095.question: Pronounced as one letter, And written with three, Two letters there are, And two only in me. I'm double, I'm single, I'm black, blue, and gray, I'm read from both ends And the same either way. What am I?

rdl_0096.question: All about, but cannot be seen, can be captured, cannot be held, no throat, but can be heard. What is it?

rdl_0097.question: What does man love more than life? Fear more than death or mortal strife? What do the poor have, what the rich require, And what contented men desire? What does the miser spend, the spendthrift save, And all men carry to their graves?

rdl_0098.question: I have hands that wave at you, though I never say goodbye. It's cool for you to be with me, especially when I say, "HI." What am I?

rdl_0099.question: What gets whiter the dirtier that it gets?

rdl_0100.question: What has no beginning, no end, and nothing in the middle?
rdl_0100.answer: A doughnut (also a donut) or an ellipse like a circle and oval.

rdl_0101.question: A skin have I, more eyes than one. I can be very nice when I am done. What am I?

rdl_0102.question: If a rooster laid a brown egg and a white egg, what kind of chicks would hatch?

rdl_0103.question: What do you serve that you can't eat?

rdl_0104.question: What starts with a T, ends with a T and has T in it?

rdl_0105.question: Which is correct to say, "The yolk of the egg are white," or "The yolk of the egg is white?"
rdl_0105.answer: Neither, because egg yolks are yellow.

rdl_0106.question: You can't keep this until you have given it. What is it?

rdl_0107.question: What question can someone ask all day long, always get completely different answers, and yet all the answers could be correct?

rdl_0108.question: Who can shave three times a day and still grow a beard?
rdl_0108.answer: A barber. He could shave other men three times a day and still grow his own beard.

rdl_0109.question: In a certain city, 5% of all the people in town have unlisted phone numbers. If you select 100 names at random from that city's phone directory, how many people selected will have unlisted phone numbers?
rdl_0109.answer: None. If their names are in the phone directory, they do not have unlisted phone numbers!

rdl_0110.question: David's father has three sons: Snap, Crackle, and _____?

rdl_0111.question: A hundred feet in the air, but it's back is on the ground. What is it?

rdl_0112.question: What has keys that open no locks, space but no room, and you can enter but not go in?

rdl_0113.question: If a train was on its way to Florida and it tipped over, where would they bury the survivors?
rdl_0113.answer: They wouldn't need to, the survivors are still alive!

rdl_0114.question: While on my way to St. Ives, I saw a man with 7 wives. Each wife had 7 sacks. Each sack had 7 cats. Each cat had 7 kittens. Kittens, cats, sacks, and wives. How many were going to St. Ives?

rdl_0115.question: My voice is tender, my waist is slender and I'm often invited to play. Yet wherever I go I must take my bow or else I have nothing to say. What am I?

rdl_0116.question: I was born in the 18th century, yet still live on today. Appearing on TV when I have something to say. Called everything from "honest" to a dirty rotten "crook", I used to wear a wig, but have had several looks. I've always had a party, but never disturb the neighbors. I've been shot at many times - major stories for the papers. What am I?
rdl_0116.answer: The Office of the President of the United States.

rdl_0117.question: Some try to hide, and some try to cheat, but time will show, and we always will meet. Try as you might, to guess my name, I promise you'll know when you I do claim. Who am I ?

rdl_0118.question: Inside a burning house, this thing is best to make. And best to make it quickly, before the fire's too much to take! What is it?

rdl_0119.question: Different lights do make me strange, thus into different sizes, I will change. What am I?
rdl_0119.answer: I am the pupil of an eye.

rdl_0120.question: Here on earth it is true, yesterday is always before today; but there is a place where yesterday always follows today. Where?

rdl_0121.question: At night they come without being fetched, And by day they are lost without being stolen. What are they?

rdl_0122.question: I never was, am always to be, No one ever saw me, nor ever will And yet I am the confidence of all To live and breathe on this terrestrial ball. What am I?

rdl_0123.question: There is a green house. Inside the green house, there is a white house Inside the white house there is a red house. Inside the red house, there are lots of babies. What is it?
rdl_0123.answer: It is a watermelon. Explanation: The skin of the watermelon is green (green house), the watermelon rind is white (white house), the watermelon flesh is red (red house), and the watermelon seeds located in the red flesh are the babies.

rdl_0124.question: A beggar's brother died, but the man who died had no brother. How could this be?

rdl_0125.question: What is bought by the yard and worn by the foot?

rdl_0126.question: I dig out tiny caves and store gold and silver in them. I also build bridges of silver and make crowns of gold. They are the smallest you could imagine. Sooner or later everybody needs my help, yet many people are afraid to let me help them. Who am I ?

rdl_0127.question: How can you physically stand behind your friend as he physically stands behind you?

rdl_0128.question: Four men were in a boat on the lake. The boat turns over, and all four men sink to the bottom of the lake, yet not a single man got wet! Why?
rdl_0128.answer: Because they were all married and not single.

rdl_0129.question: Brad stared through the dirty soot-smeared window on the 22nd floor of the office tower. Overcome with depression he slid the window open and jumped through it. It was a sheer drop outside the building to the ground. Miraculously after he landed he was completely unhurt. Since there was nothing to cushion his fall or slow his descent, how could he have survived the fall?
rdl_0129.answer: Brad was so sick and tired of window washing, he opened the window and jumped inside.

rdl_0130.question: Four men sat down to play, They played all night till the break of day. They played for gold and not for fun, With separate scores for every one. When they had come to square accounts, They all had made quite fair amounts. Can you the paradox explain, If no one lost, how all could gain?

rdl_0131.question: A black dog stands in the middle of an intersection in a town painted black. None of the street lights are working due to a power failure caused by a storm. A car with two broken headlights drives towards the dog but turns in time to avoid hitting him. How could the driver have seen the dog in time?
rdl_0131.answer: Who said this happened during the night?

rdl_0132.question: What do you use to hoe a row, slay a foe, and wring with woe?

rdl_0133.question: What can bring back the dead; make us cry, make us laugh , make us young; born in an instant yet lasts a lifetime?

rdl_0134.question: This thing runs but cannot walk, sometimes sings but never talks. Lacks arms, has hands; lacks a head but has a face. What is it?

rdl_0135.question: Violet, indigo, blue and green, yellow, orange, and red; are the colors you have seen after the storm has fled. What am I?

rdl_0136.question: It goes up, but at the same time goes down. Up toward the sky, and down toward the ground. It's present tense and past tense too, come for a ride, just me and you. What is it?

rdl_0137.question: Three mountain climbers paid a lot of money to be the first to scale a mountain. After several days of climbing they finally reached the pinnacle, and to their dismay, found a cabin and three frozen bodies. Since the mountain climbers were the first to ever climb the summit, how could this be possible?
rdl_0137.answer: They found a cabin of an airplane that had crashed there with 3 bodies in it.

rdl_0138.question: If someone says to you, "I'll bet you $1 that if you give me $2, I will give you $3 in return", would this be a good bet for you to accept?
rdl_0138.answer: No. This is a situation where you lose even if you win. Assuming the other person is being wise, they would take your $2 and say, "I lose", and give you $1 in return. You win the bet, but you're out $1.

rdl_0139.question: Never resting, never still. Moving silently from hill to hill. It does not walk, run or trot, All is cool where it is not. What is it?

rdl_0140.question: Which is heavier, a pound of feathers or a pound of gold?
rdl_0140.answer: A pound of feathers. Some would say a pound is a pound, but the fact is: Gold is a precious metal and is therefore weighed in the Troy system of measurement. This means that a pound of gold weighs only 12 oz and a pound of feathers weighs 16 oz.

rdl_0141.question: Why are 1990 dollar bills worth more than 1989 dollar bills?
rdl_0141.answer: The same reason seven dollars is more than six. Because there is one more.

rdl_0142.question: There are four girls, and four apples in a basket. Every girl takes an apple, yet one apple remains in the basket? How is this possible?
rdl_0142.answer: The answer is that one girl took the basket. She took the last apple while it was in the basket.

rdl_0143.question: Take one out and scratch my head, I am now black but once was red. What am I?

rdl_0144.question: A man takes a barrel that weighs 20 pounds and then puts something in it. It now weighs less than 20 pounds. What did he put in the barrel?
rdl_0144.answer: He put a hole in the barrel to make it weigh less.

rdl_0145.question: How many of each type of animal did Moses take on the Ark?

rdl_0146.question: Two men were playing tennis. They played five sets and each man won three sets. How can this be possible?
rdl_0146.answer: The two men were partners playing doubles.

rdl_0147.question: Some will use me, while others will not, some have remembered, while others have forgot. For profit or gain, I'm used expertly, I can't be picked off the ground or tossed into the sea. Only gained from patience and time, can you unravel my rhyme. What am I?

rdl_0148.question: When asked how old she was, Suzie replied, "In two years I will be twice as old as I was five years ago." How old is she?

rdl_0149.question: What is the easiest way to throw a ball, have it stop, and completely reverse direction after traveling a short distance?
rdl_0149.answer: Toss it straight up in the air.

rdl_0150.question: What has roots that nobody sees, and is taller than trees. Up, up it goes, and yet it never grows. What is it?

rdl_0151.question: I have four wings, but cannot fly, I never laugh and never cry; On the same spot, I'm always found, toiling away with little sound. What am I?

rdl_0152.question: You must keep this thing, its loss will affect your brothers. For once yours is lost, it will soon be lost by others. What is it?

rdl_0153.question: There's a body lying dead on a bed, and on the floor beside it is a pair of scissors. The scissors were instrumental in his death, yet there's no trace of blood. The body reveals no signs of any cuts or bruises. How could the person have been murdered with a pair of scissors?
rdl_0153.answer: The person slept on a waterbed. His killer used the scissors to cut the bed open and drown him.

rdl_0154.question: Something very extraordinary happened on the 6th of May, 1978 at 12:34 a.m. What was it?
rdl_0154.answer: At that moment, the time and day could be written as: 12:34, 5/6/78.

rdl_0155.question: A little pool with two layers of wall around it. One white and soft and the other dark and hard, amidst a light brown grassy lawn with an outline of green grass. What am I?

rdl_0156.question: Two convicts are locked in a cell. There is an unbarred window high up in the cell. No matter if they stand on the bed or one on top of the other they can't reach the window to escape. They then decide to tunnel out. However, they give up on the tunneling because it will take too long. Finally one of the convicts figures out how to escape from the cell. What is his plan?
rdl_0156.answer: His plan is to dig the tunnel and pile up the dirt to climb up to the window to escape.

rdl_0157.question: A horse travels a certain distance each day. Strangely enough, two of its legs travel 30 miles each day and the other two legs travel nearly 31 miles. It would seem that two of the horse's legs must be one mile ahead of the other two legs, but of course, this can't be true, since the horse is normal. How is this possible?
rdl_0157.answer: The horse operates a mill and travels in a circular clockwise direction. The two outside legs will travel a greater distance than the two inside legs.

rdl_0158.question: The Pope has it but he does not use it. Your father has it but your mother uses it. Nuns do not need it. Your lady friend's husband has it and she uses it. What is it?

rdl_0159.question: As I went across the bridge, I met a man with a load of wood which was neither straight nor crooked. What kind of wood was it?

rdl_0160.question: You can carry it everywhere you go, and it does not get heavy. What is it?

rdl_0161.question: A woman shoots her husband. Then she holds him underwater for over 5 minutes. Finally, she hangs him. But 5 minutes later they both go out and enjoy a wonderful dinner together. How can this be?
rdl_0161.answer: The woman was a photographer. She shot a picture of her husband, developed it, and hung it up to dry.

rdl_0162.question: A magician was boasting one day about how long he could hold his breath underwater. His record was 6 minutes. A kid who was listening said, "That's nothing, I can stay underwater for 10 minutes using no type of equipment or air pockets!" The magician told the kid if he could do that, he'd give him $10,000. The kid did it and won the money. Can you figure out how?
rdl_0162.answer: The kid filled a glass of water and held it over his head for 10 minutes.

rdl_0163.question: There is a barrel with no lid and some wine in it. "This barrel of wine is more than half full," said Curly. "No it's not," says Mo. "It's less than half full." Without any measuring implements and without removing any wine from the barrel, how can they easily determine who is correct?
rdl_0163.answer: Tilt the barrel until the wine barely touches the lip of the barrel. If the bottom of the barrel is visible then it is less than half full. If the barrel bottom is still completely covered by the wine, then it is more than half full.

rdl_0164.question: Why is swearing like an old coat?
rdl_0164.answer: Because it is a bad habit.

rdl_0165.question: Joe and Sally were sitting in their family room one night. While Joe was watching T.V, his wife Sally was reading. All of a sudden the power went out and Joe decided to go to bed, but Sally kept on reading. With no use of artificial light, Sally kept on reading. How?
rdl_0165.answer: Sally was blind, she was reading a book by Braille.

rdl_0166.question: A man was found murdered on Sunday morning. His wife immediately called the police. The police questioned the wife and staff and got their alibi. The Wife said she was sleeping. The Cook was cooking breakfast. The Gardener was picking vegetables. The Maid was getting the mail. The Butler was cleaning the closet. The police instantly arrested the murderer. Who did it and how did they know?
rdl_0166.answer: It was the Maid. She said she was getting the mail. There is no mail on Sunday!

rdl_0167.question: I am taken from a mine, and shut up in a wooden case, from which I am never released, and yet I am used by almost everybody. What am I?

rdl_0168.question: What connects two people yet touches only one?

rdl_0169.question: Why are two heads better than one?

rdl_0170.question: What is that which has many leaves, but no stem?

rdl_0171.question: What is that which goes with a carriage, comes with a carriage, is of no use to a carriage, and yet the carriage cannot go without it. What is it?

rdl_0172.question: I am the beginning of sorrow and the end of sickness. You cannot express happiness without me, yet I am in the midst of crosses. I am always in risk, yet never in danger. You may find me in the sun, but I am never out of darkness. What am I?

rdl_0173.question: Why is the letter F like an incendiary?

rdl_0174.question: Poke your fingers in my eyes and I will open wide my jaws. Linen cloth, quills, or paper, my greedy lust devours them all. What am I?

rdl_0175.question: I have a little house in which I live all alone. It has no doors or windows, and if I want to go out I must break through the wall. What am I?

rdl_0176.question: A cloud was my mother, the wind is my father, my son is the cool stream, and my daughter is the fruit of the land. A rainbow is my bed, the earth my final resting place, and I'm the torment of man. Who Am I ?

rdl_0177.question: I'm in the book, but not on any leaf; I'm in the mouth, but not in lip or teeth; I'm in the atmosphere, but never in the air; I wait on every one, but never on a pair; I am with you wherever you may go; And every thing you do I'm sure to know; Though when you did it I should not be there, Yet when 'twas done, you'd find me in the chair. What am I?

rdl_0178.question: There are four brothers in this world that were all born together. The first runs and never wearies. The second eats and is never full. The third drinks and is always thirsty. The fourth sings a song that is never good. What are the four brothers?

rdl_0179.question: There were five men going to church and it started to rain. The four that ran got wet and the one that stood still stayed dry. How did the one stay dry?
rdl_0179.answer: It was a body in a coffin with the bearers.

rdl_0180.question: It stands on one leg with its heart in its head. What is it?

rdl_0181.question: You're in a magical bathroom with no windows and the only way things can get in and out is by an open door. You decide to have a bath so you turn on the tap, you shut the door and the handle breaks so you can't open it, you then turn off the tap and the knob breaks so water keeps coming. How do you save yourself from drowning?
rdl_0181.answer: Pull out the plug in the bath.

rdl_0182.question: What number, when added separately, to 100 and 164 can make each a perfect square?
rdl_0182.answer: The answer is 125. 125+100=225 and 125+164=289. The square root of 225 is 15 and the square root of 289 is 17 .

rdl_0183.question: Why is the letter F like death?
rdl_0183.answer: Because without it life is a lie, or it makes life a lie.

rdl_0184.question: You pick it, You peel the outside, You cook the inside, You eat the outside, And throw away the inside. What is it?

rdl_0186.question: I am white, black and read all over. What am I?

rdl_0187.question: Picture three boxes containing fruit. The first box is marked peaches, the second is marked oranges, and the third box is marked peaches and oranges. Each of the boxes is labeled incorrectly. How could you label each box correctly if you were allowed to select only one fruit from one of the boxes?
rdl_0187.answer: First you select a fruit from the box marked peaches and oranges. If it was a orange you selected, you know that the box could only contain oranges. If it was a peach, you know that the box could only contain peaches since each box is incorrectly marked. If, for example an orange was selected, you would mark that box oranges and switch the other two incorrect labels around. Now all three would be correctly labeled.

rdl_0188.question: A guy was waiting at home, he swung a metal pole then took 3 left turns and on his way back home there was a masked man waiting for him. What is he doing and who is the masked man?
rdl_0188.answer: He is playing baseball and the masked man is the Catcher.

rdl_0189.question: A farmer has 17 sheep and all but 9 die. How many are left alive?

rdl_0190.question: A man went on a trip with a fox, a goose, and a sack of corn. He came upon a stream that he had to cross and found a tiny boat to use to cross the stream. He could only take himself and one other - the fox, the goose, or the corn - one at a time. He could not leave the fox alone with the goose or the goose with the corn. How does he get all safely over the stream?
rdl_0190.answer: Take the goose over first and come back. Then take the fox over and bring the goose back. Now take the corn over and come back alone to get the goose. Take the goose over and the job is done!

rdl_0191.question: A doctor and a bus driver are both in love with the same woman, an attractive girl named Sarah. The bus driver had to go on a long bus trip that would last a week. Before he left, he gave Sarah seven apples. Why?
rdl_0191.answer: An apple a day keeps the doctor away!

rdl_0192.question: NASA was considering sending canaries into space to study them under zero gravity. The project was scrapped when someone realized that in spite of having sufficient water supplies, they could die of dehydration within a few hours. Why?
rdl_0192.answer: Birds, unlike humans, need gravity to swallow. Humans can swallow even while hanging upside down.

rdl_0193.question: I'm a word that's hardly there. Take away my start, and I'm an herbal flair. What am I?

rdl_0194.question: If a fender cost six dollars, what will a ton of coal come to?

rdl_0195.question: Trains travel from one town to another town all day, always on the same track, always going nonstop and at the same speed. The noon train took 80 minutes to complete the trip, but the 4 PM train took an hour and 20 minutes. Why?
rdl_0195.answer: 80 minutes is the same as an hour and 20 minutes.

rdl_0196.question: What is the shape of a kiss?

rdl_0197.question: What is that which is less tired the longer it runs?

rdl_0198.question: What animal keeps the best time?

rdl_0199.question: There are two numbers whose product added to the sum of their squares is 109, and the difference of whose squares is 24. What are the two numbers?

rdl_0200.question: Two cops walked into a room with no windows and found a dead man who obviously hung himself from the ceiling, though they couldn't figure out how. There was no chair beneath him that he might have jumped off of, or a table. Just a puddle of water. How'd he do it?
rdl_0200.answer: He stood on a block of ice until it melted.

rdl_0201.question: My age today is three times what it will be three years from now minus three times what my age was three years ago. How old am I?
rdl_0201.answer: Don't be too confused, the answer is 18 years old.

rdl_0202.question: Two sentries were on duty outside a barracks. One faced up the road to watch for anyone approaching from the North. The other looked down the road to see if anyone approached from the South. Suddenly one of them said to the other, "Why are you smiling?" How did he know that his companion was smiling ?
rdl_0202.answer: Although the guards were looking in opposite directions, they were not back to back. They were facing each other.

rdl_0203.question: I am four letters long, I can be seen in the sky, I am the ocean & I am the sea. Can you guess me?

rdl_0204.question: A bus driver was heading down a street in Colorado. He went right past a stop sign without stopping, he turned left where there was a "no left turn" sign, and he went the wrong way on a one-way street. Then he went on the left side of the road past a cop car. Still - he didn't break any traffic laws. Why not?

rdl_0205.question: A new medical building containing 100 offices had just been completed. Mark was hired to paint the numbers 1 to 100 on the doors. How many times will Mark have to paint the number nine?

rdl_0206.question: A fireman is running to get a net under a lady who looks like she might jump off the balcony of her 20 story apartment building. There is nothing below her except a 20 story fall. The fireman is still 100 yards away when she falls and can't nearly get there in time. The woman is not hurt more than a bruise. How is that possible?
rdl_0206.answer: She fell back into her apartment, jumping from the balcony into the inside.

rdl_0207.question: No matter how little or how much you use me, you change me every month. What am I?

rdl_0208.question: A woman went to visit her bank manager and she took her young daughter with her. The bank manager said that the woman's daughter could stay with his secretary during the meeting. When the woman and her daughter left, the secretary turned to the other secretary and said to her, "That little girl was my daughter." How could that be?
rdl_0208.answer: The secretary was the girl's father.

rdl_0209.question: If you have two quarters on a table touching each other, how can you move one of the quarters without touching it? You are only allowed to touch one quarter but not move it. You cant touch the quarter that you move. You want to get at least enough room between the two quarters to insert another coin between the two quarters.
rdl_0209.answer: Hold down one of the quarters very firmly. Take another coin and hit it against the quarter you are holding down. Tap hard enough to move the quarter next to it aside.

rdl_0210.question: Mr. and Mrs. Mustard have six daughters and each daughter has one brother. How many people are in the Mustard family?
rdl_0210.answer: There are nine Mustards in the family. Since each daughter shares the same brother, there are six girls, one boy, and Mr. and Mrs. Mustard.

rdl_0211.question: Alive without breath, As cold as death, Never thirsty, Ever drinking, Clad in mail, Never clinking, Drowns on dry land, Thinks an island Is a mountain, Thinks a fountain Is a puff of air. What am I?

rdl_0212.question: As defendants, we deny all involvement in the unscrupulous dealings which have come to light in the recent government investigation. What country name is hidden in the previous sentence?

rdl_0213.question: Jenna wrote all the numbers from 300 to 400 on a piece of paper. How many times did she write the digit 3?

rdl_0214.question: This thing all things devours: Birds, beasts, trees, flowers; Gnaws iron, bites steel; Grinds hard stones to meal; Slays king, ruins town, And beats high mountain down. What am I?

rdl_0215.question: Glittering points that downward thrust, sparkling spears That never rust. what am I?

rdl_0216.question: Voiceless it cries, Wingless flutters, Toothless bites, Mouthless mutters. What is it?

rdl_0217.question: The cost of making only the maker knows, Valueless if bought, but sometimes traded. A poor man may give one as easily as a king. When one is broken pain and deceit are assured. What is it?

rdl_0218.question: Each morning I appear to lie at your feet, all day I will follow no matter how fast you run, yet I nearly perish In the midday sun. What am I?

rdl_0219.question: Pregnant every time you see her, yet she never will give birth. What is she?

rdl_0220.question: Die without me, Never thank me. Walk right through me, Never feel me. Always watching, Never speaking. Always lurking, Never seen. What am I?

rdl_0221.question: What is that which the dead and living do at the same time?

rdl_0222.question: We are five little objects of an everyday sort. You will find us all in a tennis court. What are we?

rdl_0223.question: Of no use to one Yet absolute bliss to two. The small boy gets it for nothing. The young man has to lie for it. The old man has to buy it. The baby's right, The lover's privilege, The hypocrite's mask. To the young girl, faith; To the married woman, hope; To the old maid, charity. What am I?

rdl_0224.question: I look flat, but I am deep, Hidden realms I shelter. Lives I take, but food I offer. At times I am beautiful. I can be calm, angry and turbulent. I have no heart, but offer pleasure as well as death. No man can own me, yet I encompass what all men must have. What am I?

rdl_0225.question: I go around in circles, but always straight ahead never complain, no matter where I am led. What am I?

rdl_0226.question: There once was a book that was only owned by the wealthy, but now everyone can have it. You can't buy it in a bookstore or take it from a library. What book is it?

rdl_0227.question: Stealthy as a shadow in the dead of night, Cunning but affectionate if given a bite. Never owned but often loved. At my sport considered cruel, But that's because you never know me at all. What am I?

rdl_0228.question: Weight in my belly, Trees on my back, Nails in my ribs, Feet I do lack. What am I?

rdl_0229.question: Ten Men's Strength, Ten Men's Length, Ten Men can't break it, Yet a young boy walks off with it What am I?

rdl_0230.question: A thousand colored folds stretch toward the sky, Atop a tender strand, Rising from the land, 'Til killed by maiden's hand, Perhaps a token of love, perhaps to say goodbye. What am I?

rdl_0231.question: Two bodies have I, though both joined in one. The more still I stand, the quicker I run. What am I?

rdl_0232.question: I have a hundred legs, but cannot stand, a long neck but no head; I ease the maid's life. What am I?

rdl_0233.question: I do not breathe, but I run and jump. I do not eat, but I swim and stretch. I do not drink, but I sleep and stand. I do not think, but I grow and play. I do not see, but you see me every day. What am I?

rdl_0234.question: Tool of thief, toy of queen. Always used to be unseen. Sign of joy, sign of sorrow. Giving all likeness borrowed. What am I?
rdl_0234.answer: A mask. Why each line points to a mask: Tool of thief: Masks help conceal identity, a classic tool for thieves who don’t want to be recognized. Toy of queen: Masks are used in masquerade balls and royal pageantry; a “toy” here suggests ceremonial or playful use by nobility. Always used to be unseen: A mask hides what’s underneath—the face—so it’s “used to be unseen” by design. Sign of joy, sign of sorrow: Theater masks symbolize emotions (comedy and tragedy), making them visual signs of joy and sorrow. Giving all likeness borrowed: Wearing a mask lets you “borrow” another appearance or persona, replacing your own likeness with a new one.

rdl_0235.question: If you break me, I'll not stop working. If you can touch me, my work is done. If you lose me, you must find me with a ring soon after. What am I?

rdl_0236.question: Why is a bullet like a tender glance?

rdl_0237.question: At the sound of me, men may dream or stomp their feet at the sound of me, women may laugh or sometimes weep. What am I?

rdl_0238.question: Runs over fields and woods all day Under the bed at night sits not alone, With long tongue hanging out, Awaiting for a bone. What am I?

rdl_0239.question: My head bobs lazily in the sun. You think I'm cute, For my face is yellow, My hair is white, and my body is green. What am I?

rdl_0240.question: Large as a mountain, small as a pea, Endlessly swimming in a waterless sea. What am I?

rdl_0241.question: I am, in truth, a yellow fork From tables in the sky By inadvertent fingers dropped The awful cutlery. Of mansions never quite disclosed And never quite concealed The apparatus of the dark To ignorance revealed. What am I?

rdl_0242.question: A man had a bar of lead that weighed 40 lbs., and he divided it into four pieces in such a way as to allow him to weigh any number of pounds from one to forty. What are the weights of the four pieces?
rdl_0242.answer: 1, 3, 9, 27, are the weights of the four pieces.

rdl_0243.question: When young, I am sweet in the sun. When middle-aged, I make you gay. When old, I am valued more than ever. What am I?

rdl_0244.question: Four people are sitting around a campfire after a long day of recreation when one man comments: "Do you realize that around this campfire, the four of us include a mother, father, brother, sister, son, daughter, niece, nephew, aunt, uncle and a couple of cousins"?. If everyone is related by blood (with no unusual marriages) how is this possible?
rdl_0244.answer: The campfire circle includes a woman and her brother. The woman's daughter and the man's son are also present.

rdl_0245.question: I drive men mad For love of me, Easily beaten, Never free. What am I?

rdl_0246.question: Ripped from my mother's womb, Beaten and burned, I become a blood-thirsty slayer. What am I?

rdl_0247.question: You will find me with four legs, but no hair. People ride me for hours, but I don't go anywhere. Without needing to be tugged, jerked or turned on, I always manage to be ready for work. What am I?

rdl_0248.question: What is the best key to a good dinner?

rdl_0249.question: Robert and David were preparing to have a water balloon fight. "No Fair" cried Robert, "You have 3 times as many as I do!" David said "Fine!" and gave Robert 10 more balloons. "Still not fair!" argued Robert, "You still have twice as many as I do." How many more balloons must David give Robert for them to have the same number?
rdl_0249.answer: David must give Robert another 20 water balloons, giving them each 60. Robert started with 30 water balloons and David with 90.

rdl_0250.question: What can climb mountains, cross streams, handle hundreds of feet each day, yet never moves? What is it?

rdl_0251.question: A dagger thrust at my own heart, Dictates the way I'm swayed. Left I stand, and right I yield, To the twisting of the blade. What am I?

rdl_0252.question: Can a man legally marry his widow's sister in the state of California?
rdl_0252.answer: NO since she is a 'widow', the guy's dead!

rdl_0253.question: Before Mount Everest was discovered, what was the highest mountain on Earth?

rdl_0254.question: A man builds a house with all 4 sides facing south. A bear walks past the house. What color is the bear?
rdl_0254.answer: White, the house is built directly on the North Pole.

rdl_0255.question: I'm not an airplane, but I can fly through the sky. I'm not a river, but I'm full of water. What am I?

rdl_0256.question: If there are fifteen crows on a fence and the farmer shoots a third of them, how many crows are left?
rdl_0256.answer: None. The rest of the crows flew away when they heard the gunshot.

rdl_0257.question: If two's company and three's a crowd, what are four and five?

rdl_0258.question: In a tunnel of darkness lies a beast of iron. It can only attack when pulled back. What is it?

rdl_0259.question: Why is a farm-yard like a hotel?
rdl_0259.answer: It is generally patronized by gobblers.

rdl_0260.question: In what year did Christmas Day and New Year's Day fall in the same year?

rdl_0261.question: Is an old hundred-dollar bill better than a new one?

rdl_0262.question: Some months have 30 days while other months have 31 days. How many have 28 days?
rdl_0262.answer: Every month has a 28th so they all have 28 days.

rdl_0263.question: There is a clerk at the butcher shop, he is five feet ten inches tall, and he wears size 13 sneakers. He has a wife and 2 kids . What does he weigh?

rdl_0264.question: What can't be burned in fire, nor drowned in water?

rdl_0265.question: What clothing does a house wear?

rdl_0266.question: What kind of room has no windows or doors?

rdl_0267.question: What didn't Adam and Eve have that everyone else has?

rdl_0268.question: What do you throw out when you want to use it but take in when you don't want to use it?

rdl_0269.question: I only have two backbones and thousands of ribs. What am I?

rdl_0270.question: I look at you, you look at me, I raise my right, you raise your left. What am I?

rdl_0271.question: If you have it, you want to share it. If you share it, you don't have it. What is it?

rdl_0272.question: Why did the duck get fired from his Easter job?

rdl_0273.question: If you were running a race, and you passed the person in 2nd place. What place would you be in now?

rdl_0274.question: What is one thing that all wise men, regardless of their politics or religion, agree is between heaven and earth?

rdl_0275.question: What is often returned but never borrowed?

rdl_0276.question: If you were to put a coin into an empty bottle and then insert a cork into the neck, how could you remove the coin without taking out the cork or breaking the bottle?
rdl_0276.answer: Push the cork into the bottle and shake the coin out!

rdl_0277.question: How do you send Easter Cards?

rdl_0278.question: A certain large animal lives happily and thrives here on Earth. One day, every single one of these critters is wiped out by a mysterious disease that affects only this particular animal. There are none left anywhere on earth -- they are all gone. About a year or so later, they begin to reappear on Earth again. How can this be?
rdl_0278.answer: The animal is the Mule. Since all Mules are born sterile, you can only get a Mule by crossing a donkey with a horse. That is how the species is able to repopulate itself.

rdl_0279.question: This object can be driven, but has no wheels, and can also be sliced and remain whole. What is it?

rdl_0280.question: What word is that to which if you add a syllable, it will make it shorter?

rdl_0281.question: Which of the following statements are true, and which are false? 1. Only one of the statements is false 2. Exactly two of the statements are false. 3. Only three of the statements are false. 4. Exactly four of the statements are false. 5. All five of these statements are false.
rdl_0281.answer: The only true statement can be #4. The others are false. #5 can't be true, because it says all the statements are false.

rdl_0282.question: There is a dead man in the center of a field. He carried with him an unopened package. As he neared the center of the field, he knew he was going to die. How did he know he was going to die?
rdl_0282.answer: The man's parachute did not open.

rdl_0283.question: In a stable there are men and horses. In all, there are 22 heads and 72 feet. How many men and how many horses are in the stable?

rdl_0284.question: My first is a very uncomfortable state, In cold weather it mostly abounds. My second's an instrument formed of hard steel, That will cause the stout foe to stagger and reel, And when used, is a symptom of hate. My whole is an author of greatest renown, Whose fame to the last day of time will go down. Who am I?

rdl_0285.question: The names of three trees are hidden in the sentences below. The letters are in consecutive order. Can you find them? On this farm, we get ham from a hog any time. The farmer will help in every possible way. He faced two very similar choices, both bad.

rdl_0286.question: Lazy Larry agreed to work on a job for his brother-in-law for thirty hours at eight dollars an hour, on the condition that he would forfeit ten dollars per hour for every hour that he idled. At the end of the thirty hours Larry wasn't owed any money and didn't owe his brother-in-law any money either. How many hours did Larry work and how many hours did he idle?
rdl_0286.answer: Lazy Larry worked 16-2/3 hours and idled 13-1/3 hours. 16-2/3 hours, at $8.00 an hour amounts to the same amount as 13-1/3 hours at $10.00 per hour.

rdl_0287.question: You want to boil a two-minute egg. If you only have a three-minute timer (hourglass), a four-minute timer, and a five-minute timer, how can you boil the egg for only two minutes?
rdl_0287.answer: Once the water is boiling, turn the three-minute timer and five-minute timer over. When the three-minute timer runs out, put the egg in the boiling water. When the five-minute timer runs out, two minutes have elapsed and it is time to take the egg out of the water. You don't need the four-minute timer for this riddle.

rdl_0288.question: How can you make a needle float?
rdl_0288.answer: Take a thin piece of tissue paper and place the tissue paper under the needle before putting the needle in the water. The tissue paper will eventually sink and the needle will remain floating.

rdl_0289.question: What is the longest and yet the shortest thing in the world; the swiftest and yet the slowest; the most divisible and the most extended; the least valued and the most regretted; without which nothing can be done; which devours every thing, however small, and yet gives life and spirits to every object, however great ?

rdl_0290.question: What has six faces, but does not wear makeup, has twenty-one eyes, but cannot see? " What is it ?"

rdl_0291.question: In the grocery store, Sal met his only daughter's only husband's mother-in-law's only mother-in-law. Who was she?
rdl_0291.answer: Sal's mother. (His son-in-law's mother-in-law was his wife; her mother-in-law was Sal's mother.)

rdl_0292.question: What English word has three consecutive double letters?

rdl_0293.question: I usually wear a yellow coat. I usually have a dark head. I make marks wherever I go. What am I?

rdl_0294.question: You have 14 brown socks, 14 blue socks and 14 black socks in your sock drawer. How many socks must you remove (without looking to be sure) to have a matched pair?
rdl_0294.answer: Four. You will have a pair of one color or another.

rdl_0295.question: If 10 bags of jelly beans and 6 licorice sticks cost $1, and 10 licorice sticks and 6 jelly bean bags cost 92 cents. How much does one licorice stick cost?
rdl_0295.answer: 5 cents while Jelly bean bags cost 7 cents.

rdl_0296.question: If a stopper and a bottle cost $2.10 and the bottle costs $2.00 more than the stopper. Then what does the stopper cost?

rdl_0297.question: Robert and David played several golf matches against each other in a week. They played for a pizza at each match, but no pizzas were purchased until the end of the week. If at any time Robert and David had the same number of wins, those pizzas were canceled. Robert won four matches (but no pizzas), and David won three pizzas. How many rounds of golf were played?
rdl_0297.answer: Eleven, David won 7 matches, 4 to cancel out Robert's 4 wins, and 3 more to win the pizzas.

rdl_0298.question: Lynn likes grapes but not potatoes. She likes squash but not lettuce, and she likes peas but not onions. Following the same rule, will she like pumpkins or apples?
rdl_0298.answer: Pumpkins. Lynn only likes things that grow on vines.

rdl_0299.question: Why are beautiful women like bread?

rdl_0300.question: Why is an avaricious man like one with a short memory?
rdl_0300.answer: Because he is always for getting.

rdl_0301.question: David is throwing Robert a surprise birthday party but he has to stay within his budget. He spent half of his money plus $2.00 on the cake. Half of what he had left plus $2.00 was spent on balloons and streamers. Then he spent half of what he had left plus $1.00 on candy. Now he is out of money, how much did he start with?
rdl_0301.answer: This one is best solved working backwards, the last part David spent half of what was left plus $1.00 on candy and then was out of money. That means he must have spent $2.00 on Candy as $1.00 was half of what he had using the same logic backwards: $2.00 on candy $6.00 on Balloons and Streamers $12.00 on the cake Total of $20.00.

rdl_0302.question: Janie's friends were chipping in to buy her a wedding shower present. At first, 10 friends chipped in, but 2 of them dropped out. Each of the 8 had to chip in another dollar to bring the amount back up. How much money did they plan to collect?

rdl_0303.question: What does the Easter Bunny do after it takes a shower?

rdl_0304.question: What river in Bavaria answers the question, Who is there?

rdl_0305.question: I went into the woods and got it. I sat down to seek it. I brought it home with me because I couldn't find it. What is it?

rdl_0306.question: In a pond, there are some flowers with some bees hovering over them. If both the following statements are true: 1. If each bee lands on a flower, one bee doesn't get a flower. 2. If two bees share each flower, there is one flower left out. How many flowers and bees are there?

rdl_0307.question: Why is a man with wooden legs like one who has an even bargain?
rdl_0307.answer: Because he has nothing to boot.

rdl_0308.question: I have ten or more daughters. I have less than ten daughters. I have at least one daughter. If only one of these statements is true, how many daughters do I have?
rdl_0308.answer: If I have any daughters, there will always be two statements which are true. Therefore, I have no daughters.

rdl_0309.question: Other than being colors, what do the words orange, silver, and purple have in common?
rdl_0309.answer: There are no words in the English language that rhyme with them.

rdl_0310.question: If the only frying pan in the house is large enough to cook two pancakes at a time and pancakes take one minute to brown one side, how can you make three pancakes in three minutes?
rdl_0310.answer: Pour two pancakes and brown the first side. After the first side is done, flip one, take the second off, and pour the third pancake. After another minute, take the first one off, flip the third one, and put the second one back on. Cook both pancakes until finished.

rdl_0311.question: I am a perching barrel, filled with meat, Taking hits from leaps and dives. Look inside, but do not eat, The meat in there is still alive! What am I?

rdl_0312.question: Lauren and Alice are talking long distance on the phone. Lauren is in an East-Coast US state which borders the Atlantic Ocean, and Alice is in a West-Coast state which borders the Pacific Ocean. Lauren asks Alice: "What time is it?" Alice replies and Lauren says: "That's really odd. It's the same time here!" How can this be?
rdl_0312.answer: Alice is in Eastern Oregon (in Mountain time) and Lauren is in Western Florida (in Central time). It is the night that daylight-savings time changes back to standard time any time after 1:00 and before 2:00 AM.

rdl_0313.question: My voice rises above the din, sometimes catching all unaware. I never ask questions, yet get many answers. What am I?

rdl_0314.question: Why is a parish bell like a good story?

rdl_0315.question: A man is late for an appointment and, in his haste, takes a corner so fast that only two wheels were on the pavement. A policeman is standing on the corner, but he did not give him a ticket. Why?

rdl_0316.question: I herald the darkness which descends on all creatures; You will know my approach by moans and wracked features. I visit the hippo, hyena, and horse, But never go near snails and spiders, of course. I would circle the globe, leaping one to the other, Should all the world's people ever clasp hands together. What am I?

rdl_0317.question: There is a certain family with both girl and boy children. Each of the boys has the same number of brothers as he has sisters. Each of the girls has twice as many brothers as she has sisters. How many boys and girls are there in this family?

rdl_0318.question: A man left an inheritance of $10,000 to three relatives and their wives. Together the wives received $3960. Janine received $100 more than Cathy, and Maria received $100 more than Janine. Joe received the same amount as his wife, Hary got half as much again as his wife, and Tom received twice as much as his wife. How much did each receive?
rdl_0318.answer: Carthy, Janine and Maria received $1220, $1320, and $1420 respectively. Joe received the same as his wife Carol, $1220. Hary received half again what his wife Janine did, $1980. Tommy got twice as much as his wife Maria, $2840.

rdl_0319.question: In camps about the centre I appear; In smiling meadows seen throughout the year; The silent angler views me in the streams, And all must trace me in their morning dreams, First in the mob conspicuous I stand, Proud of the lead, and ever in command. What am I?

rdl_0320.question: The head of a whale is six feet long; his tail is as long as his head and half his body, and his body is half of his whole length. How long is the whale?

rdl_0321.question: They can trickle down, They can tickle too. Or make you sneeze, Or comfort you. Their rustling sound, you've rarely heard, Unless you're a pillow or a bird! What are they?

rdl_0322.question: A hundred stones are placed, in a straight line, a yard distant from each other. How many yards must a person walk, who undertakes to pick them up, and place them in a basket stationed one yard from the first stone?
rdl_0322.answer: In solving this question it is clear that to pick up the first stone and put it into the basket, the person must walk two yards, one in going for the stone and another in returning with it; that for the second stone he must walk four yards, and so on increasing by two as far as the hundredth, when he must walk two hundred yards, so that the sum total will be the product of 202 multiplied by 50, or 10,100 yards. If any one does not see why we multiply 202 by 50 in getting the answer, we refer him to his arithmetic.

rdl_0323.question: A man buys a rope from a woman for $3.00 and hands the woman a $10 bill. The woman goes into the grocery store next door to get change. She returns and gives the man $7.00. After the man leaves, the clerk from the store comes and says, "Hey, that was a counterfeit bill you gave me." The woman gives the clerk a good bill. How much has the woman lost?

rdl_0324.question: My first is a part of the day, My last a conductor of light, My whole to take measure of time, Is useful by day and by night. What am I?

rdl_0325.question: I can trap many different things and colors, ever-changing, not boring. Look closely and you may find yourself also caught in my trap. What am I?
rdl_0325.answer: A mirror, or a pool of water.

rdl_0326.question: It runs and runs but can never flee. It is often watched, yet never sees. When long it brings boredom, When short it brings fear. What is it?
rdl_0326.answer: Time, which is often watched when you stare at a clock.

rdl_0327.question: I am a word of three syllables, each of which is a word; my first is an article in common use; my second, an animal of uncommon intelligence; my third, though not an animal, is used in carrying burdens. My whole is a useful art. What am I?

rdl_0328.question: Here on Earth, it's always true, that a day follows a day. But there is a place where yesterday always follows today! Where?

rdl_0329.question: Find the four digit number in which the first digit is one fourth of the last digit, the second digit is 6 times the first digit, and the third digit is the second digit plus 3. What is it?

rdl_0330.question: What is so fragile that when you say its name you break it?

rdl_0331.question: When I am filled I can point the way, When I am empty nothing moves me, I have two skins, one without and one within. What am I?

rdl_0332.question: John was very tired after a long day of work. He went to bed at 10 p.m., wound his alarm clock, and set it for noon the next day. Since John fell asleep almost immediately, how many hours of sleep did he get before the alarm woke him?
rdl_0332.answer: Two hours. Wind-up clocks can't be set more than 12 hours in advance.

rdl_0333.question: An officer wishing to arrange his men in a solid square found by his first arrangement that he had 39 men left over. He then started increasing the number of men on a side by one, but found that 50 additional men would be needed to complete a new square. How many men did the officer have?
rdl_0333.answer: The officer had 1975 men. When he formed a square measuring 44 by 44, he had 39 men over. When he tried to form a square 45 x 45, he was 50 men short.

rdl_0334.question: I am four times as old as my daughter. In 20 years time I shall be twice as old as her. How old are we now?
rdl_0334.answer: I am 40 and my daughter is 10.

rdl_0335.question: Why is a nail, fast in the wall, like an old man?

rdl_0336.question: Why does a miller wear a white hat?

rdl_0337.question: My head and tail both equal are, My middle slender as a bee. Whether I stand on head or heel Is quite the same to you or me. But if my head should be cut off, The matter's true, though passing strange Directly I to nothing change. What Am I?

rdl_0338.question: There is a bus full of people travelling to San Francisco and no one gets off the bus throughout the journey. But when it gets to the other side there is not a single person left. How is this possible?

rdl_0339.question: I'm fatherless and motherless and born without sin. Roaring when entering the world, I never speak again. What am I?

rdl_0340.question: You can find roads without cars, And roam through forests without trees, Cities exist without houses? Whatever can I be?

rdl_0341.question: Squeeze me and I cry tears as red as flesh, but my heart is made of stone. What am I?

rdl_0342.question: What is that which is invisible, but never out of sight?

rdl_0343.question: I go up and down the stairs without moving. What am I?

rdl_0344.question: Why do you paint eggs on easter ?
rdl_0344.answer: It's a lot easier than wallpapering them!

rdl_0345.question: A professional fisherman caught 30 fish during a 5-day tournament. Each day, he caught three more fish than the day before. How many fish did the fisherman catch on the first day?
rdl_0345.answer: He didn't catch any fish the first day, but he caught 3 on the second day, 6 on the third day, 9 on the fourth day and 12 on the fifth day.

rdl_0346.question: Two hours ago it was as long after one o'clock in the afternoon as it was before one o'clock in the morning. What time is it now?
rdl_0346.answer: It would be 9:00 pm. There are 12 hours between 1:00 pm and 1:00 am and half of that is six hours. Half-way between would be 7 o'clock. Two hours later it would be 9:00 o'clock.

rdl_0347.question: What is 1/2 of 1/4 of 2/9 of 3/7 of 84?

rdl_0348.question: When is a boat like a knife?
